phase: Phase 1 and Phase 2 frontend stabilization with backend and AI/ML preparation

workstreams.name: Frontend platform
workstreams.mission: Stabilize the React/Vite shell so feature work can happen without route, provider, proxy, or API-client conflicts.
deliverables: Vite proxy includes every existing backend route used by the frontend.
App shell has stable router, providers, layout, and navigation.
Shared loading, error, empty, and data-mode components exist.
API client is provider-neutral and ready for schema validation.
acceptanceChecks: npm run dev starts the React app on port 3000.
Profile and history requests can reach Express through Vite.

workstreams.name: Frontend feature screens
workstreams.mission: Move page logic into feature folders and build the English dashboard experience in the shared visual direction.
deliverables: Dashboard resembles the reference screen: sidebar, weather card, scan crop CTA, market CTA, crop health cards, and AI insight card.
Each route delegates to a feature-owned screen.
Mock and fixture data are clearly labeled.
Visible UI copy is English and provider-neutral.
acceptanceChecks: Feature code lives primarily under src/features.
No new Gemini or OpenAI branding appears in UI copy.

workstreams.name: Backend API preparation
workstreams.mission: Prepare route contracts and identify ahead-of-plan backend modules without changing runtime behavior during frontend stabilization.
allowedPaths: server/** after the frontend stability gate
avoidPaths: runtime backend behavior during Phase 1 and Phase 2
deliverables: Route inventory for current Express endpoints.
Request and response examples for frontend-used routes.
Plan for market, schemes, NDVI, and voice modules: keep behind flag, park, or defer.
Draft API v1 endpoint map for the grounded advisory workflow.
acceptanceChecks: No new backend feature dependency is introduced into the frontend.
Compatibility expectations are documented before implementation.

workstreams.name: AI and ML preparation
workstreams.mission: Audit the checked-in disease model and prepare safe AI contracts before OpenAI implementation begins.
avoidPaths: server/src/routes/** unless coordinated with backend owner
deliverables: Model input, preprocessing, label order, and confidence-unit audit.
Model manifest proposal with version, thresholds, labels checksum, and rejection behavior.
Accepted, low-confidence, and unsupported-image fixture expectations.
OpenAI structured explanation draft that cannot include chemical dosage fields.
acceptanceChecks: Low-confidence and unsupported-image cases are defined.
OpenAI is treated as an explanation layer, not a rule engine.
